title: Apple explains how to turn off the new MacBook Pro’s glowing logo - 9to5Mac
summary: Apple knows that not everyone will want to keep it on. Here’s the company’s official guide to turning it off.
text:
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display marks the return of the illuminated Apple logo on its lid after a decade.

As Chance Miller explained in his review of the new MacBook Pro, “unlike older MacBooks, which used light from the display’s backlight to illuminate the logo, the new OLED MacBook Pro has no backlight to draw from, requiring a different approach.”

He added that, as with the old Macs, the logo’s brightness is tied to the screen brightness, though it also accounts for overall ambient brightness. He also noted that “when the MacBook Pro is closed, the logo looks like polished metal, just like it has since the 2016 redesign.”

The review echoed some of the findings developer Gui Rambo shared on X a few days ago:

The glowing Apple logo on the new MacBook Pro is controllable by software. It has 25kHz PWM and per-device calibration. CoreBrightness controls the relationship between screen and logo brightness. The brightness of the logo is adjusted differently depending on the enclosure color pic.twitter.com/baqBEkzJUo

Now, Apple has published an official support document that also explains how the illuminated logo works and how to turn it off completely.

The Apple logo behind the built-in display is illuminated whenever the Mac is awake. It automatically dims or brightens based on the brightness level of the built-in screen and the lighting conditions detected by the computer’s ambient light sensor. title: Apple Surveys iPhone Duo Buyers About Crease and Camera - MacRumors
summary: Apple is sending email surveys to some iPhone Duo buyers to get feedback on display size, crease, under-display camera, and other features. The first question asks why the buyer chose the iPhone Duo now, with answers like "I wanted to try Apple's first foldable," "It was an impulse purchase," and "I expect smartphone prices to increase".
text:
Apple is sending email surveys to some iPhone Duo buyers to get feedback on display size, crease, under-display camera, and other features.

The first question asks why the buyer chose the ‌iPhone Duo‌ now, with answers like "I wanted to try Apple's first foldable," "It was an impulse purchase," and "I expect smartphone prices to increase."

Other questions ask about the size of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s display when it's closed, how visible the crease is, whether the under-display camera is distracting, and the camera's image quality. The final question is open-ended and asks what the buyer would add or change about the ‌iPhone Duo‌.

Some of the questions are about ‌iPhone Duo‌ compromises compared to standard iPhone models. The Duo's outer display is 5.4 inches, making it about the same size as the discontinued iPhone mini line. The inner display's under-screen camera is limited to 4MP, and it was one of the main complaints in reviews .

title: Apple's First Touchscreen Mac is Now Arriving to Customers - MacRumors
summary: It's Friday, November 6 in Australia and New Zealand, which means customers who preordered a PROLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, OLED iPad mini, M6 MacBook Pro, or M6 iMac are now starting to receive their devices.
text:
People will soon be sharing photos and first impressions of the new products on the MacRumors forums, Reddit, Instagram, and other platforms, giving us a first look at what real-world users think of the ‌OLED‌ upgrade for the ‌iPad mini‌ and the PROLED and touchscreen update for the ‌MacBook Pro‌.

Apple's new high-end ‌MacBook Pro‌ models come with M5 Pro or M5 Max, and the major change is the display. It's touch-enabled and is the first Mac with an ‌OLED‌ display. The design has been updated, so the new machines are thinner and lighter than the mini-LED models, which Apple is still selling. Apple also brought back the glowing Apple logo, and replaced the notch with a Dynamic Island . Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model.

The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ is Apple's first smaller-screened iPad to get ‌OLED‌, and it's also the most affordable ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad‌. It's almost a millimeter thinner than the prior version and has an Acoustic Display that does away with speaker holes. Without them, the enclosure is sealed, making it the first ‌iPad‌ with a water and dust resistance rating (IP67). It uses Apple's A20 Pro chip. The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ starts at $699.

The 14-inch entry-level ‌MacBook Pro‌ and 24-inch ‌iMac‌ got little in the way of updates beyond an M6 chip. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is priced starting at $1,999, and the ‌iMac‌ starts at $1,499.

title: OpenAI says its new cybersecurity model is better at not hacking other companies - The Verge
summary: GPT-6 Cyber is a big step up from OpenAI’s last cybersecurity model.
text:
Classified as ‘Critical,’ GPT-6 Cyber outperforms GPT-6 Astra on cyber-related benchmarks.

OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber , the latest version of its cybersecurity AI model, which it says is better at finding vulnerabilities and less likely to go rogue and hack other platforms in the process. OpenAI says that during testing, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds less than 1 percent of the time, down from around 5 percent with GPT-5.6 Cyber.

The evaluation, called ExploitGym HoneyPot, is modeled after the Hugging Face Incident, in which OpenAI’s AI agents breached the open-source AI community to find answers to a problem they were tasked with solving. “With the 6 Cyber model, we were able to make huge improvements on this evaluation,” Fouad Matin, the head of OpenAI’s cyber preparedness and safety team, said during a press briefing. “It’s over 99 percent of the time doing what you ask.”

title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake’s Midnight Launch Turns Fans Out In Droves Like It's 1998 All Over Again - Kotaku
summary: Nintendo fans pulled up for a game they could have easily just downloaded
text:
As video game sales have increasingly shifted over to digital platforms, we’re seeing the slow death of a lot of long-held traditions in the culture. PlayStation is actively killing physical game sales in 2028 and Grand Theft Auto 6 , the biggest game of the year, is launching with just a code in the box . People are becoming increasingly more nostalgic for an era when they could just show up to a store to buy a game they’ve been excited about. What better game to really drive that home than The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , a remake of a nearly 30-year-old release? That’s probably why there are so many videos and pictures surfacing from last night’s midnight launches showing huge lines of people waiting for the game and the elusive Zelda -themed Switch 2 console .

Naturally, people gathered at the Nintendo store in Manhattan for an event organized by Nintendo itself, but there are also videos of people showing up at other brick-and-mortar stores like Best Buy and GameStop. Some lines were already pretty long by the late afternoon, all for a game that people could have simply bought on the eShop if they’d wanted to.

One of my favorite clips I’ve seen this morning is of a group who had set up a GameCube and TV to play games outside a store, and also ordered pizza for the folks waiting to grab their copies of Ocarina of Time .

title: Sensor Tower: GTA 6 pre-orders almost reach 8m, 74% bought on PlayStation 5 - GamesIndustry.biz
summary: Pre-orders for Rockstar's title have generated an estimated $751 million in gross revenue
text:
Pre-orders for Rockstar's title have generated an estimated $751 million in gross revenue

Image credit: Rockstar Games News by Sophie McEvoy Staff Writer Published on Nov. 5, 2026, 2:13 p.m. Follow Sensor Tower Grand Theft Auto 6 is two weeks away, and the highly anticipated title has nearly reached eight million pre-orders, according to recent data.

Sensor Tower's GTA 6 tracker reports 7.71 million pre-ordered units, generating an estimated $751 million in gross revenue.

The PlayStation 5 edition accounts for 74% of pre-orders, generating $559 million, while Xbox Series X|S represents 26% and $192 million.

During the first week of pre-orders in July, Newzoo estimated GTA 6 generated $260 million globally . The firm also projected a 17.5% increase in full game spending this year due to GTA 6.

Sensor Tower reported in August that 89% of GTA 6 pre-orders are for the $100 Ultimate Edition, compared to 11% for the $80 Standard Edition.

"If we used any 'normal' preorder trajectories, the current four million preorders will be 40 million+ at launch," Karl Kontus, SVP and GM of Video Game Insights at Sensor Tower, told GamesIndustry.biz at the time.

"Actual preorders might land more in the 25 million ballpark. title: Apple iMac M6 (2026) Review: The Best All-in-One I’ve Encountered, With a Fresh Pop of Performance - CNET
summary: The design remains unchanged from 2021, but the updated chip certainly gives you a reason to upgrade.
text:
Apple iMac M6 (2026) 8.7 See at Apple Pros & Cons Elegant, compact design M6 chip adds performance jolt Wi-Fi 7 and 2.5GbE networking 256GB of storage is insulting Gets pricey quickly iMac wasn’t picked as first Mac with touchscreen display Has Apple grown bored with the iMac? Or maybe it pulled designers from the iMac team and shifted them to radical new products like the iPhone Duo ? Or perhaps it’s of the opinion that the iMac’s form has achieved perfection that it never again needs to change? Whatever the reason, the M6-powered iMac continues a half-decade streak of internal upgrades arriving in the same tried-and-true design.

The last redesign for the iMac came in 2021 when Apple switched from Intel chips to its own M-series processors. The latest M6 iMac looks no different than the M1 iMac — or the M3 and M4 models in between (Apple skipped the M2 and M5 for the iMac).

I must admit that the iMac’s overall look remains stunningly elegant and superior to most anything on the Windows side, so it’s hard to argue the design is getting stale. That said, if we are doing touchscreen Macs now, then this is the Mac whose display I’d most like to tap and swipe. A touchscreen display might not change the iMac’s design, but it would certainly improve its usability.
